analysis.title: SpaceX: Update and raise target to $268 - Terrestrial AI build and enterprise broadband add to Orbital AI thesis; Outperform
key_insights: Bernstein raises its SpaceX (SPCX) price target to $268 from $248 and keeps Outperform. The increase comes mainly from higher AI revenue (more terrestrial compute capacity and higher $/watt pricing), partly offset by a lower AI multiple (17x from 21x) and higher capex.

Bernstein now models terrestrial AI compute capacity of 2.8GW at end-2026, 12.8GW at end-2027 and 20.1GW at end-2028. The prior 2027 estimate was about 8GW. Capex is assumed at $35bn per additional GW.

Management said compute pricing is tracking above the $30-50 per watt range of recent deals. Bernstein raises its average price per watt for compute to $26 in 2027, declining gradually afterward, and notes its forecast is well below what the company describes.

The company now projects a revenue run rate of $500bn to $1tn exiting 2027, mostly from terrestrial compute. Bernstein's 2028 revenue estimate is $424bn and its 2031 estimate rises to $784bn from $655bn.
Q3 results beat consensus: diluted EPS $0.35 vs consensus $0.15, revenue $14.58bn vs $12.88bn, segment operating income $2.79bn vs $1.21bn. AI capex was $16.44bn vs consensus $16.90bn.
Q4 capex is guided to $35-40bn vs consensus of about $22bn, and Q1 revenue is guided to $33-37bn (midpoint $35bn) vs consensus of roughly $23bn.

Management said payback periods on compute investment are currently below one year and could fall to about six months next year. Bernstein says this should ease concerns that capex builds capacity ahead of demand.

Connectivity revenue was $5.25bn vs consensus $4.86bn, with a 45% operating margin vs 38% consensus. Enterprise & Government revenue rose 91% in the quarter, with about 12,000 aircraft under contract and deals with at least 46 airlines.

Starlink consumer subscribers reached 13.6m in Q3 (+1.6m sequentially). Sequential growth slowed to 13% from 17%, making the prior 17m subscriber goal look unlikely. ARPU rose to $69 on favorable mix.

Starship: Flight 15 is expected within a few weeks and will try to catch both booster and second stage, which Musk put at better than a 50% chance. A successful flight sets up the first full reuse on Flight 16. The heat shield performed well on Flight 14.

The company targets one Starship launch per week by end of 1H27 and two per week by end of 2027, with five operating launch pads. A second-stage re-fly is targeted for early 2027 and on-orbit refuelling early that year.

The first orbital data center launch is targeted for late 2027, with operations beginning mid-2028. Orbital data centers were not discussed on the call, and the company said its pre-IPO roadmap has not changed materially.

SpaceX is reportedly in talks for access to 80,000 Crown Castle towers. Bernstein estimates a US mobile network build, including spectrum, would cost more than $100bn over six to eight years and still prefers an MVNO deal with one of the big three telcos. Bernstein makes no assumption for the tower deal or for a Tesla merger.

Terafab (chip fabrication) targets first test chips in 2027 and volume production by Q3 2028. Bernstein calls these targets very aggressive. Industrial gas turbine blades are the power bottleneck, and Bernstein understands SpaceX will not produce usable castings before 2028.

Valuation is a sum of the parts on 2031 EBITDA: AI at 17x and a 35% discount rate, Connectivity at 15x and 25%, Space at 13x and 15% (raised from 10%). The total discounted value is $3.50tn, giving the $268 target, 82% above the $147.49 close on 23 Oct 2026.
Bernstein raises its 2026 and 2027 adjusted EPS estimates to -$0.01 and $1.44 from -$0.19 and $1.37.

market_movers.rationale: Target raised from $248 on higher terrestrial AI compute capacity and $/watt pricing, partly offset by a lower AI multiple (17x from 21x) and higher capex. Implies 82% upside from $147.49.

sector_views.rationale: Bernstein sees Starship reusability, Starlink Enterprise & Government growth and AI compute as supporting a path to far higher revenue, with AI the dominant source of value.

earnings_insights: Q3 2026 reported (SpaceX): diluted EPS $0.35 vs consensus est $0.15; revenue $14.58bn vs consensus est $12.88bn; segment operating income $2.79bn vs consensus est $1.21bn.

Q3 2026 reported segment revenue: Space $1.77bn vs consensus est $1.43bn; Connectivity $5.25bn vs consensus est $4.86bn; AI $7.56bn, about 20% above consensus. Segment operating income: Space -$7m vs consensus est -$323m; AI $431m vs consensus est -$14m.
Q3 2026 reported Connectivity operating margin 45% vs consensus est 38%. AI capex reported at $16.44bn vs consensus est $16.90bn; Space capex $1,606m vs consensus est $1,519m.
Guidance: Q4 2026 capex $35-40bn vs consensus est about $22bn. Q1 2027 revenue $33-37bn (midpoint $35bn) vs consensus est roughly $23bn.

Bernstein estimates: adjusted diluted EPS -$0.01 for 2026E (old -$0.19) and $1.44 for 2027E (old $1.37). Revenue $54.5bn for 2026E and $241.9bn for 2027E. Adjusted EBITDA $27.1bn for 2026E and $136.3bn for 2027E.
Consensus FY29 SpaceX revenue is about $290bn per the report, vs Bernstein's 2029E of $499bn.

trade_ideas.rationale: AI segment, driven by terrestrial compute capacity and pricing, is the dominant source of value, and the company's plans are well above Bernstein's estimates.
trade_ideas.risk: Capex building capacity ahead of demand, lower AI comparable multiples, execution on Starship reuse, uncertainty in the Space segment.

risk_factors: Capex over the next two years could build capacity ahead of demand.
Compute pricing is expected to decline as supply catches up with demand, and the medium to long-term supply/demand balance is debated.
AI-oriented stock valuations have contracted and are volatile, which lowers the AI segment valuation.
Starship reusability, including the second-stage heat shield and the Flight 15 catch attempt, is the linchpin for long-term growth and orbital data centers.
Bottlenecks in industrial gas turbine blades, and uncertain transfer of SpaceX's rocket casting capability to turbine blades.
Terafab chip targets are very aggressive and the company is just beginning chip fabrication.
A US mobile network build could cost more than $100bn over six to eight years.
Consumer subscriber growth slowed to 13% sequentially, making the 17m subscriber goal look unlikely.
Bernstein raised the Space segment discount rate to 15% from 10% to reflect increased uncertainty.

vol_and_positioning: SPCX closed at $147.49 on 23 Oct 2026 against a 52-week range of $104.83 to $225.64, with a market cap of $2.03tn. Performance was -0.6% over 1 month vs -1.1% for the SPX.
Valuations of AI-oriented stocks have fallen over the last two months, lowering Bernstein's AI peer multiple to 17x forward EV/EBITDA from 21x.

tension_points.bull_case: Management says payback periods are below one year and could fall to six months next year. Pricing is tracking above $30-50 per watt, and Q1 revenue guidance of $33-37bn is well above consensus of about $23bn.
tension_points.bear_case: Some investors worry capex over the next two years builds capacity ahead of demand. Bernstein notes compute supply and demand balance over the medium to long term is debated, and it assumes pricing declines as supply catches up.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Compute pricing falling toward or below Bernstein's $26 per watt 2027 assumption, or capacity going unsold as Q4 capex of $35-40bn comes online.

theme_stances.key_argument: Higher terrestrial capacity and better $/watt pricing materially raise the SpaceX revenue path, though Bernstein's pricing remains below the company's description.
theme_stances.evidence: We now assume a total of 13GW of terrestrial compute by the end of 2027

theme_stances.key_argument: Full Starship reusability is the most important factor for long-term growth and orbital data centers, and progress appears to be going well.
theme_stances.evidence: Reusability is key to making orbital data centers successful.
